thread:
Marta: Heads-up — finance asked for a hardware recommendation for a fintech customer wanting a Private VPC: 100k monthly inference requests, 30% peak traffic around months-end, mostly short chat turns (~60 tokens/respond). Need cost + GPU-hour estimate.

Raj: Do we have their qps distribution? 100k/month => avg ~38 r/s but bursts matter.

Marta: They sent this: peak 650 r/s sustained for ~3 hours/day across 3 days each month (reconciliation windows). Typical concurrency 2 per session.

Evan: Rough ballpark: for chat with 60 tokens output + 20 tokens input = 80 tokens total. On A100-80GB on our runtime, we see ~3500 tokens/s per GPU for small batches; translates to ~43 requests/s per GPU at 80 tokens/request (worst-case).

Sophie: So peak 650 r/s / 43 ~= 15 GPUs required to meet peak with headroom. Add 20% buffer for headroom -> 18 GPUs. For 3h/day * 3 days = 9h/month at peak. But baseline traffic rest of month also consumes GPU-hours.

Alina: Can we run a quick calc? Baseline avg r/s outside peak = (100k - peak_volume)/seconds. Peak_volume = 650 * 3600 * 9 = 21,060,000 requests — wait that's wrong units. Need to compute in requests/month.

Raj: Let's do it stepwise: Peak window total requests = 650 r/s * 3600 s * 9 h = 650 * 32400 = 21,060,000 requests (that's correct). But total monthly requests target is 100,000 — oh, they must mean 100k users, not requests. Marta double-check?

Marta: Sorry my bad — it's 100k users, not requests. They estimate 3 requests per user/month avg => ~300k requests/month. Peak windows still hold.

Evan: OK 300k/month, peak windows produce 650 * 3600 * 9 = 21M requests — that can't be, so their peak numbers must be concurrent sessions, not sustained every second for 9 hours. Reconfirming with customer now.

Marta: Customer clarified: 650 concurrent sessions during a 3-hour reconciliation window, but average request rate per session ~0.3 req/s (human-driven). So peak r/s ~= 650 * 0.3 = ~195 r/s.

Sophie: Great. Use 195 r/s as peak. At 43 r/s per GPU -> 195/43 = 4.5 -> 5 GPUs for peak. Add 30% for spikes + KV cache inefficiencies => 7 GPUs.

Alina: Monthly GPU-hours calc: baseline avg r/s = (300k total requests - peak_window_requests)/seconds_outside_peak. Quick estimate: peak_window_requests = 195 * 3600 * 3 = 2,106,000 requests. That exceeds 300k — hmm still inconsistent.

Raj: Seems the 300k/month is wrong given these rates. We should push for the single source of truth: either total monthly reqs or concurrency/time profile.

Marta: Sent a follow-up asking for analytics export. Meanwhile, let's produce two sizing options (conservative and cost-optimized) based on plausible scenarios so finance can see tradeoffs.

Evan: Option A (conservative): assume 200 r/s sustained during 3h/day for 10 days/month (heavy ops) + baseline 15 r/s otherwise. Peak sizing -> 200/43 = 4.7 -> round up 6 GPUs with 30% buffer => 8 GPUs. Monthly hours = 8 GPUs * (10 * 3 + (30*24 - 30) hours) approximated. I'll provide tidy numbers.

Sophie: Option B (cost-optimized): rely on autoscaling + burst to hosted fallback for overflow. Target baseline with 3 GPUs, scale to 6 GPUs for peaks. Requires cross-model fallback and customer ok with best-effort latency.

Alina: Evan, can you paste the calc snippet we can put in the guide?

Evan: Sure — quick pseudocode:
// inputs
peak_rps = 200
peak_hours_per_month = 30 // example
baseline_rps = 15
gpu_rps = 43
buffer = 1.3

peak_gpus = ceil((peak_rps / gpu_rps) * buffer)
baseline_gpus = ceil((baseline_rps / gpu_rps) * buffer)
monthly_gpu_hours = peak_gpus * peak_hours_per_month + baseline_gpus * (24*30 - peak_hours_per_month)

Marta: Perfect. Add cost assumptions: A100-80GB reserved cost equivalent -> $2.1/hr estimate (placeholder), H100 on prem might be 1.4x perf but 1.8x cost. We'll call out perf/cost tradeoffs.

Raj: Also note networking: customer will have VPC with max egress 10 Gbps. For payloads ~2KB per request, 200 rps * 2KB = 400 KB/s ~ 3.2 Mbps — trivial. But recon jobs might send batched logs. Flag to network team for testing.

Sophie: Consider model quantization: with int8 we can often get 1.8-2x throughput; then GPUs needed drop. Add that into the guide as an optimization path (requires customer approval for accuracy regression).

Alina: I'll draft a short one-pager: recommended baseline configs, peak headroom calc, fallback options, and a checklist for customer analytics export and network validation.

Marta: Thanks. @deploy-bot can you schedule a capacity-run runbook review with infra-ops next Wednesday?

deploy-bot: Calendar invite sent to infra-ops, eng-infra, and customer-success for 2026-05-20 16:00 UTC.

Raj: SGTM. Once we have real telemetry, we can finalize a SKU pack (3/6/9 GPU tiers) and a monthly GPU-hour proforma for finance.

Evan: I'll also throw together a quick spreadsheet with tiered scenarios (low/expected/high) and commit it to the internal sizing templates folder.

Marta: Great work everyone — will post the draft one-pager here when ready. :thumbsup:
